key_insight: IMCBench shows that multimodal medical LLMs can describe images well yet still give unsafe or uncertain guidance, so clinical performance must be judged on more than accuracy alone.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark highlights the need for safer, more realistic evaluation of AI tools used in patient-facing triage and decision support.
method: Built IMCBench with real public clinical images plus synthetic patient profiles.
Simulated multi-turn patient-clinician conversations grounded in images and EHR context.
Scored 8 frontier multimodal models on safety, accuracy, and appropriate uncertainty using calibrated LLM-as-jury ratings.
evidence_signal: Across four model families, Claude Opus 4.6 scored highest overall (3.61/5), with safety dropping when visual input or EHR context was removed.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on synthetic profiles and LLM-based judging, results may not fully capture real-world clinical complexity or deployment risk.
paper_title: IMCBench: A benchmark for multimodal LLMs in Image-grounded Medical Conversations
